chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If something from the urine of a cat hits the garment, then prayer is not valid in it until you wash it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if a cat's urine touches one's clothes?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific juristic status of the cat (sinwar) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing its urine as a purifier of the body but requiring washing of garments for valid prayer. It reflects the broader scholarly discussion on whether the cat is considered 'pure' (tahir) in all aspects or if its excrement necessitates purification of the worn clothing, a nuance often debated among maraji'.
